scoring_justification: The paper's headline results are a combination of threshold crossings and relative orderings that can be verified directly from the agent's produced data tables. Absolute numerical values may shift between different DFT codes and pseudopotentials, so checking structural properties (κ_l < 5 W/mK, ordering between materials, max ZT > 0.5, n-type > p-type) provides a robust verification that does not depend on exact numerical reproduction.

outputs.description: Lattice thermal conductivity of monolayer ZrSe2 and HfSe2 from 300 K to 1000 K. The checker verifies structural consistency and trend adherence based on the paper's findings (details hidden).

Thermoelectric figure of merit ZT as a function of carrier concentration at 600 K for p-type and n-type monolayer ZrSe2 and HfSe2. The checker verifies structural consistency and trend adherence based on the paper's findings (details hidden).

output_contract.notes: The checker performs structural/trend audits on the output files; reward is proportional to compliance.

hidden_assets.purpose: threshold values for kappa and ZT derived from the paper's reported trends
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper states room-temperature κ_l ≈ 1.2–1.8 W/mK, concluding 'low lattice thermal conductivity' (well below 5 W/mK); optimal ZT values ~0.87–0.95, all above 0.5, with n-type outperforming p-type
hidden_assets.generation_method: thresholds chosen generously above paper's own values to absorb toolchain spread (e.g., κ_l < 5 W/mK ensures only realistic reproductions pass, ZT > 0.5 sets a floor substantially below the paper's maxima)
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: all thresholds directly reflect the paper's qualitative conclusions and are not arbitrary; they are used as inequality checks, not as exact gold values
